newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil edges up as arbitrage buyers move in.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil edges up as arbitrage buyers move in.

text.p: American arbitrage buyers moved into the European fuel oil market on Thursday, bidding prices up despite crude's sharp fall on Wednesday, traders said.

The arbitrage to New York harbour and the U.S. Gulf coast was open for all cracked grades, but especially high sulphur. Italy's 250,000 tonne low sulphur buying spree this week also bolstered low sulphur sentiment.

Coastal fixed a vessel to carry 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil from Talin to the U.S. Gulf coast to sail on Dec 3, shipbrokers said. This joins at least four other cargoes heading westward, mostly Russian from the Baltic.
Dealers saw supply from Russia extending out to Dec 5 at least, and said there were no indications that a winter export ban was imminent, dealers said.
"If there was no Russian, the market would just be even tighter than it is," a trader said.

High sulphur cracked cargoes started out lower at $115/116 cif NWE, but prices lifted when an arbitrage trader bid $112 fob Coryton for a Dec 3-5 cargo and $114 for a 15,000 tonne top-up fob Brofjorden.
High sulphur barges recovered from an early sell-off to end the day steady at $113-115 fob Rotterdam.
